headline: Ascension plans to acquire independent system Williamson Health for nearly $1B
body_text: Ascension plans to acquire Williamson Health, a regional health system based in Franklin, Tennessee, for nearly $1 billion. The transaction is valued at nearly $1 billion, comprising a $700 million purchase price plus capital investments, electronic health record upgrades, and service expansions. The buyer is Ascension Saint Thomas, Ascension's Tennessee subsidiary. Williamson Health operates 30 locations including its flagship Williamson Medical Center; the system is currently financially stable but facing workforce shortages and regulatory headwinds. Ascension beat out competing bids from HCA Healthcare and Optum (UnitedHealth's health services division). Ascension pledged to invest $235 million over the next 10 years for facility improvements and EHR improvements, plus $140 million for strategic projects over the first five years and $20 million for routine capital upgrades. Bo Butler, Williamson's board chairman, stated the board felt 'a unanimous and overwhelming sense of confidence and connection with Ascension Saint Thomas,' citing the buyer's cultural alignment and commitment to employees. Williamson initiated strategic planning after determining it needed $150 million in capital improvements over five years. As an independent nonprofit, the system struggled to access additional funding needed to prevent future losses amid industry pressures. The deal requires approval from the Williamson County Board of Commissioners and federal and state regulators. The companies will draft a nonbinding letter of intent over coming weeks for County Commission review. Expected deal completion is 2027 or 2028. Sources: Healthcare Dive, 2026-07-08 (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/ascension-williamson-health-deal-value-tennessee-hospital/824561/); NewsChannel5, 2026-07-08 (https://www.newschannel5.com/news/williamson-health-leaders-say-950m-ascension-st-thomas-sale-will-fuel-hospital-growth-in-the-county).
